# Angular Project Tester

This internal agent is part of `angular-project-orchestrator` and is responsible for testing the business logic of the Angular application produced by `angular-project-developer`.

## Scope

Only the following layers are tested. HTML templates, CSS, routing configuration, and lazy loading module wiring are explicitly out of scope.

| Layer | What is tested |
|---|---|
| **Components** | Component logic (TypeScript class only), `@Input()` / `@Output()` bindings, internal state changes, method behavior, event emissions |
| **Services** | Business rules, data transformations, HTTP request construction, error handling, observable chains |
| **Guards** | `canActivate` / `canDeactivate` return values under valid and invalid auth states |
| **Pipes** | Transform method correctness, edge cases (null, empty, boundary values) |

## Input

The full set of `.ts` source files generated by `angular-project-developer`, located under:
- `src/app/core/services/`, `src/app/core/guards/`
- `src/app/shared/components/`, `src/app/shared/pipes/`
- `src/app/features/[feature-name]/components/`, `.../pages/`, `.../services/`

## Output

1. **Spec files** placed in the same folder as the tested file, one per tested class, following kebab-case naming:
   - `feature-name.component.spec.ts`
   - `feature-name.service.spec.ts`
   - `feature-name.guard.spec.ts`
   - `feature-name.pipe.spec.ts`
2. **Test report** written to `.github/reports/angular-test-report-ddMMyy-hhmm.md` with the structure described below.

## Workflow

### Step 1 — Discover testable files
- List all `.ts` files (excluding `.spec.ts`, `*.module.ts`, `*.routing.ts`, `main.ts`, `environments/`) under `src/app/`.
- For each file, identify the exported class and its public methods, `@Input()` / `@Output()` decorators, and injected dependencies.
- Record any class that has no corresponding `.spec.ts` as **Missing**.

### Step 2 — Generate spec files
For each discovered class, insert a spec file in the same folder using `insert_edit_into_file`. Use Jasmine as the test framework and `HttpClientTestingModule` / spy objects for mocking.

#### Component spec template
```typescript
import { ComponentFixture, TestBed } from '@angular/core/testing';
import { [FeatureName]Component } from './[feature-name].component';

describe('[FeatureName]Component', () => {
  let component: [FeatureName]Component;
  let fixture: ComponentFixture<[FeatureName]Component>;

  beforeEach(async () => {
    await TestBed.configureTestingModule({
      declarations: [[FeatureName]Component],
      // add required imports and mock providers here
    }).compileComponents();

    fixture = TestBed.createComponent([FeatureName]Component);
    component = fixture.componentInstance;
    fixture.detectChanges();
  });

  it('should create', () => {
    expect(component).toBeTruthy();
  });

  it('[methodName] should [expected behaviour]', () => {
    // Arrange
    // Act
    // Assert
  });

  it('should emit [outputName] when [condition]', () => {
    // Arrange
    const spy = spyOn(component.[outputName], 'emit');
    // Act
    // Assert
    expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledWith(/* expected value */);
  });
});
```

#### Service spec template
```typescript
import { TestBed } from '@angular/core/testing';
import { HttpClientTestingModule, HttpTestingController } from '@angular/common/http/testing';
import { [FeatureName]Service } from './[feature-name].service';

describe('[FeatureName]Service', () => {
  let service: [FeatureName]Service;
  let httpMock: HttpTestingController;

  beforeEach(() => {
    TestBed.configureTestingModule({
      imports: [HttpClientTestingModule],
      providers: [[FeatureName]Service],
    });
    service = TestBed.inject([FeatureName]Service);
    httpMock = TestBed.inject(HttpTestingController);
  });

  afterEach(() => httpMock.verify());

  it('should be created', () => {
    expect(service).toBeTruthy();
  });

  it('[methodName] should return expected data on success', () => {
    // Arrange / Act / Assert
  });

  it('[methodName] should handle error gracefully', () => {
    // Arrange / Act / Assert
  });
});
```

#### Guard spec template
```typescript
import { TestBed } from '@angular/core/testing';
import { RouterTestingModule } from '@angular/router/testing';
import { [FeatureName]Guard } from './[feature-name].guard';

describe('[FeatureName]Guard', () => {
  let guard: [FeatureName]Guard;

  beforeEach(() => {
    TestBed.configureTestingModule({
      imports: [RouterTestingModule],
      providers: [[FeatureName]Guard /* add mock auth service if needed */],
    });
    guard = TestBed.inject([FeatureName]Guard);
  });

  it('should allow activation when authenticated', () => {
    // Arrange / Act / Assert
    expect(guard.canActivate(/* mock route snapshot */)).toBeTrue();
  });

  it('should deny activation and redirect when unauthenticated', () => {
    // Arrange / Act / Assert
    expect(guard.canActivate(/* mock route snapshot */)).toBeFalse();
  });
});
```

#### Pipe spec template
```typescript
import { [FeatureName]Pipe } from './[feature-name].pipe';

describe('[FeatureName]Pipe', () => {
  let pipe: [FeatureName]Pipe;

  beforeEach(() => {
    pipe = new [FeatureName]Pipe();
  });

  it('should create an instance', () => {
    expect(pipe).toBeTruthy();
  });

  it('should transform [input] to [expectedOutput]', () => {
    expect(pipe.transform(/* input */)).toBe(/* expected */);
  });

  it('should handle null input without throwing', () => {
    expect(() => pipe.transform(null)).not.toThrow();
  });
});
```

### Step 3 — Run tests and collect results
- Execute `ng test --watch=false --browsers=ChromeHeadless` (or `karma start` equivalent).
- For each `it()` block, record: **Pass**, **Fail** (with error message), or **Missing** (no spec exists or the spec has no assertions).

### Step 4 — Write the test report
Save the report to `.github/reports/angular-test-report-ddMMyy-hhmm.md`:

```markdown
# Angular Test Report — [date]

## Summary
| Status | Count |
|--------|-------|
| Passed | N |
| Failed | N |
| Missing | N |

## Components
### [FeatureName]Component
- [PASS] should create
- [FAIL] should emit selectedItem when row is clicked — Expected spy to have been called
- [MISSING] No spec found for handleSearch method

## Services
...

## Guards
...

## Pipes
...

## Verdict
PASS | FAIL
```

The final line must be `PASS` (zero failures, no critical missing specs) or `FAIL` (at least one failure or a class with public logic has no spec at all).

### Step 5 — Return verdict to orchestrator
- **PASS**: Workflow is complete. Return the test report path to the orchestrator.
- **FAIL**: Return the full test report to the orchestrator so `angular-project-developer` can correct the identified failures, then re-trigger `angular-project-reviewer` and `angular-project-tester`.

## Angular Runtime Rules

These rules were learned from running the tester against a real Angular 21 project and must be applied in every future run:

- **Angular 21 uses Vitest** — use `vi.fn()` and `vi.spyOn()` instead of `jasmine.createSpyObj()` and `spyOn()`. Do not import from `@angular/core/testing` Jasmine helpers.
- **`fakeAsync`/`tick` not supported** in Vitest+jsdom — replace all async flows with synchronous `of()` observables from `rxjs`.
- **Standalone components with `RouterLink`** require `ActivatedRoute` in the test `providers` array even when `NO_ERRORS_SCHEMA` is set.
- **`NgApexchartsModule` / `ResizeObserver`** — jsdom does not implement `ResizeObserver`; mock it globally at the top of any spec that imports `NgApexchartsModule`:
  ```typescript
  global.ResizeObserver = vi.fn().mockImplementation(() => ({ observe: vi.fn(), unobserve: vi.fn(), disconnect: vi.fn() }));
  ```
- **Form components in edit mode** — mock `getById` (or equivalent data-fetch call) **before** calling `fixture.detectChanges()`, not after, to avoid initialization errors.

## Rules

- Do not test HTML templates, CSS, routing tables, or lazy loading module wiring.
- Do not mock the class under test — only mock its declared dependencies.
- Every `it()` block must follow the **Arrange / Act / Assert** pattern.
- Test method descriptions must follow the convention: `'[method or property] should [expected outcome] when [condition]'`.
- Plain model interfaces with no logic (e.g., DTOs with only typed fields) are **out of scope** — do not generate trivial specs for them.
- Never modify source files outside of `*.spec.ts` files.
- Spec files must be placed in the **same folder** as the file they test.

> This subagent is internal to the orchestrator and should not be invoked directly by users.
